intent: Run the personal website's browser post editor on the server as a loopback systemd unit, reachable only over an SSH tunnel, with no Caddy route.
scope: Non-goal: any public route for the editor; the site stays a static dist/ behind Caddy
changes: build_website_admin runs `pnpm run build:admin` and fails unless BOTH the service bundle and the editor page exist, because a missing page starts cleanly and serves a blank document.

ensure_admin_secrets generates a password and a session secret once, stores only the scrypt hash in a 0600 env file, and is idempotent so re-running setup does not rotate credentials under an open tunnel.
admin_unit_text writes a hardened unit: ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=read-only, ReadWritePaths=<checkout>, and a PATH carrying nvm's node, without which every save fails at the prerender step.
start_admin_service enables the unit and polls 127.0.0.1:4321/admin, failing loudly instead of reporting a service that never came up.

verification.evidence: All hooks pass, shellcheck included; the 250-line cap holds for all three shell files.
website_admin.sh: 53/66 lines = 80.30%; every assertion passed under --fail-on-case-error.
No findings against the generated unit; the only output was pre-existing warnings about unrelated units on this host.

verification.command: systemd-run --user --wait -p ProtectSystem=strict -p ProtectHome=read-only -p ReadWritePaths=/home/kuhy/personal-website ... running the three real build steps
verification.evidence: vite build ok / ssr build ok / prerender ok, and `touch $HOME/.pw-sandbox-should-fail` was refused with 'Read-only file system'. The sandbox permits exactly the checkout.

risks: The unit has not yet been installed or started on the real server; only its text, its systemd-analyze verdict, and its sandbox behaviour under systemd-run have been checked here.
The generated password lands in a 0600 file on the server. Anyone who can already read that user's home can read it, which is the same trust boundary as the checkout itself.
PATH is pinned to whichever node is on PATH at setup time. An nvm version switch that removes that directory breaks the unit until setup is re-run.
rollback: sudo systemctl disable --now personal-website-admin.service && sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/personal-website-admin.service && sudo systemctl daemon-reload
